_what: Fixed-BRL exit menu over the conveyor's families (same machinery as b3/config/exit_menu.json, b3/exit_menu.py --config). Owner 2026-11-20: 'vamos comecar a testar estrategias com um take profit stop loss... uma base para comecar de ganho R$ 35 e perda de R$ 90'. B1 is the owner's base; B2-B5 are one step away on one side (target 30/40, stop 80/100) and exist ONLY to check the plateau, as the neighbours of B1. WIN only: on WDO R$ 35 is 7 ticks and the measured cost is about 20% of it (see the conveyor's batch 1). Registered before any read; every (variant, exit) read is counted in ops/state/exit_brl/ledger.jsonl and in the run report.
families: the families that had at least one candidate in the V-based exit menu runs (research/b3/exit_menu/ and ops/state/exit_menu/): a prior from the same data, so this is NOT a blind search; the list is passed with --families-file and printed in the report

B1.what: owner's base: target R$ 35, stop R$ 90, 60 min

random_control.only_for: versions that pass every other check (saves time; the control is part of the selection)

selection.plateau: at least 2/3 positive among: the variants one grid step away on one parameter (same timeframe, same exit) and the same variant with the neighbouring exits (B1: four neighbours, so 3 of 4)
selection.beats_random: mean net per trade > the random control's mean net (same exit)
selection.pick: per family and market, the passing version with the highest total net per year; the list goes to the owner, who decides which go to the Clear demo
selection._250: the owner (2026-11-18) puts profit of one rule above frequency, as in the P-026 study

honesty: A R$ 90 stop against a R$ 35 target needs about 75% winners just to break even at the measured cost (R$ 3.67 per round trip on WIN). The V-based menu's high-hit exit (S2) had 65-68%. Candidates here are demo candidates only, never evidence; validation stays unread.
